item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 122335
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sat Sep 12 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula.

Central and Western East Pacific (EP97):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with an area of low pressure
located several hundred miles southwest of the southwestern coast of
Mexico remain disorganized. Environmental conditions appear
conducive for development, and a tropical depression is expected to
form during the next couple of days while it moves generally
west-northwestward to westward over the central and western portions
of the eastern Pacific basin. For more information, including gale
warnings, please see the High Seas Forecast issued by the National
Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure located several hundred miles
southeast of Hilo, Hawaii, is producing disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Development of this system, if any, is expected to
be slow to occur while it drifts generally west-northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

&&

High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sat Sep 12 2026 
913 
WTPZ34 KNHC 130248
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
500 PM HST Sat Sep 12 2026
 
...NORBERT CONTINUES TO WEAKEN...
...NOW EXPECTED TO DISSIPATE WELL EAST OF HAWAII BY THE MIDDLE OF 
NEXT WEEK...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.9N 130.5W
ABOUT 1375 MI...2215 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 1610 MI...2595 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was
located near latitude 17.9 North, longitude 130.5 West. Norbert is
moving toward the west near 12 mph (19 km/h), and this motion is
expected to continue during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Little change in strength is forecast during the next 24 hours, 
followed by a gradual weakening trend. Norbert is forecast to 
degenerate into a remnant low by Tuesday and dissipate by Wednesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sat Sep 12 2026 
840 
WTPZ44 KNHC 130248
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
500 PM HST Sat Sep 12 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Norbert's convective organization 
has degraded during the past several hours. The convective mass over 
and north of the circulation center has diminished in coverage, with 
cloud-top temperatures also warming. This appears to be due, at 
least in part, to some mid-level dry air becoming entrained into the 
circulation along with some southwesterly vertical wind shear. An 
earlier scatterometer pass showed an asymmetric system with peak 
winds just above 40 kt located over the northern semicircle. The 
subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB and objective 
estimates from UW-CIMSS remain in decent agreement, ranging from 35 
to 50 kt. Given these data and the decreased organization, the 
initial intensity is lowered to 40 kt.

Norbert's initial motion is estimated to be westward, or 280/10 kt. 
The storm remains positioned south of a subtropical ridge extending 
westward from northern Mexico, which should steer Norbert on a 
general west-northwestward to westward track for the remainder of 
the forecast period. The track guidance remains in fairly good 
agreement, and the NHC track forecast is largely unchanged, 
reflecting a blend of the previous forecast and the latest 
multi-model consensus (HCCA) and Google DeepMind ensemble, which lie 
slightly north of the previous track.

The track will bring the cyclone deeper into a hostile environment 
dominated by strong westerly vertical wind shear and dry mid-level 
air. These environmental conditions will induce a steady weakening 
trend by 36 h. Model guidance unanimously reflects this hostile 
setup showing Norbert opening into a trough of low pressure east of 
Hawaii by middle portion of next week. Consequently, the updated NHC 
intensity forecast accelerates the decay timeline, degenerating 
Norbert to a remnant low by 72 h and dissipating it by 96 h.
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
